transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?
Hello, Dr. Smith. I feel like I’ve lost the drive to do anything or be around people, and it’s getting harder and harder to talk or care about things the way I used to.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy, and has this been happening nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes, I've lost interest in almost everything I used to enjoy, like church events, community yoga, and baseball games. This feeling of being completely blank and having no drive has been happening nearly every day for over two years now, ever since I graduated high school.
Have you had any periods lasting at least several weeks where you felt clearly better and back to your usual self during these past two years?
No, I haven't had any times where I felt back to my usual self. It has just been a continuous, gradual shutting down ever since I graduated, without any breaks or periods of feeling better.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F32, F33], which correspond to single and recurrent depressive episodes. However, the patient reports a continuous, low-grade depressed mood lasting for over two years without any symptom-free intervals or periods of remission, and onset shortly after high school graduation. This chronic course without recovery periods makes episodic mood disorders like F32 and F33 unlikely. The presentation is more consistent with a chronic mood disturbance of mild to moderate severity lasting over two years, which aligns with the ICD-10 criteria for dysthymia (persistent mood disorder, coded as F34.1).

Personality-related patterns (F60) are considered given the possible chronicity implied by 'getting harder and harder,' though more information is needed. No previous candidates were provided, so this is the initial differential.
